Variants.Content: The Sunset Sea unfolds along the western coast of Westeros, its tides linking the Iron Islands, Fair Isle, Lannisport, the Arbor, and many lesser harbors. Ironborn longships treat it as a highway, while folk along the western shore live by its fish, salt, and sea trade even as they watch for sails emerging out of the mist. Beyond the familiar coast to the west, reliable charts and provisioning ports quickly dwindle; tales of distant islands, sunken fleets, and the edge of the world thus never cease to grow. The Sunset Sea is no blank border, but an expanse well known to coastal folk, feared by deep-sea mariners, and still never wholly mastered by any crown.

The ironborn regard the Sunset Sea as a road left by their forebears, where wind, reefs, and tide-races are more trustworthy than boundary stones ashore. A man who can read the sea need not see land to know how far he is from home.
Folk of the western coast draw fish, wine routes, and profit from the sea, yet light warning beacons whenever a strange sail appears. To them the sea is both granary and an unbarred frontier.
Explorers see renown in the west, scholars see uncharted waters, and the devout see mystery. The oldest captains usually see only the need to stow a few more casks of water.
